Claire — thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier. I put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused specifically on the procurement / vendor onboarding milestone so we have clear owners and dates. High-level recap below and next steps.

Call highlights:
- Bluehaven will onboard Redwood as a vendor through Coupa (procurement portal).
- Procurement needs the vendor form, completed W-9, and banking info to complete setup.
- Internal approvals (security + legal) look straightforward based on the product scope we discussed.

Proposed MAP milestone (vendor onboarding):
1) Supplier registration submitted to Coupa — owner: Bluehaven Procurement — target: 2026-07-02
2) Redwood completes vendor form + upload W-9 & bank letter — owner: Redwood (Rishi) — target: 2026-06-30
3) Procurement validation / AML checks — owner: Bluehaven Procurement — target: 2026-07-07
4) System-of-record setup (Ariba/Coupa vendor ID & payment terms) — owner: Bluehaven Finance — target: 2026-07-10
5) Final contractual signature / PO issuance — owner: Bluehaven / Redwood (legal & procurement) — target close: 2026-07-15

Open questions / dependencies:
- Which portal steps require our legal team (redlines) vs. standard vendor form?
- Does Bluehaven require a specific remittance/corporate banking template or will an ACH letter suffice?
- If Coupa requires an NAICS/SIC code, please confirm the exact code to use.

Attachments: I’ve attached the draft MAP and a vendor form template for your convenience. Can you (or procurement) confirm the supplier registration URL you want us to use and whether the W-9 you’ll need is the standard US W-9?

Next step: Claire, if procurement can confirm the portal link and the preferred target date for registration, I’ll upload the completed form and W-9 to the portal and start the DocuSign for the SOW.

Thanks — Rishi

--

Rishi — thank you, this is very clear and helpful. We use Coupa for supplier onboarding (not Ariba) — I should have said that on the call.

Procurement notes:
- Portal link: https://coupasupplier.bluehaven.com/register/supplier
- We need the completed vendor form + company W-9 (PDF). I’ve attached the W-9 we have on file for completeness — looks good; please re-send if your tax info differs.
- Banking: we accept an ACH remittance letter signed by an authorized officer. Our finance team will request bank verification during their validation step.

I’ve looped in Fernando from procurement to handle the Coupa intake and timeline. Our goal is to have vendor records created before the PO issuance.

Subject: Supplier registration / Coupa steps (info)

Rishi — I’m Fernando from Bluehaven procurement. Quick note on required items and the typical schedule once a supplier is submitted: 

Required fields/files for Coupa registration:
- Legal company name, DBA (if any), tax ID/EIN
- Completed vendor form (PDF)
- Signed W-9 (if US entity)
- ACH remittance letter or bank verification file
- Primary contact name/email and billing address
- NAICS code (optional but speeds classification)

Typical timeline after submission:
- Day 0: Submission into Coupa portal
- Day 1-2: Procurement intake & basic validation
- Day 3-5: Finance verification / AML checks
- Day 6-9: Vendor ID creation and payment terms assignment

If you can upload the vendor packet today (Rishi), we can push to get the vendor ID created by 2026-07-07. For banking details, we do not accept screenshots of statements — please provide an official bank letter or voided check.

Regards,
Fernando Cruz
